# Retail Store Associate Copilot — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Retail Store Associate Copilot
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 18 captured build checkpoints; 4 skills; 2 knowledge files; 6 acceptance checks; 4 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm tenant licensing and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved store environment, publisher prefix and maker access. Confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model is available; keep the workshop synthetic and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded store documents, the proposed catalog, inventory and review connections and the channel; document blocked paths, never bypass them. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always authentication trigger; record who may build, test and later use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for the read-only commerce catalog, store inventory and the approved manager review workflow. No customer connection is needed for the synthetic workshop. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare store associate, floor specialist, sales manager and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: Copilot Studio in the browser and the reviewed files. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and PAC CLI 2.9.3 or newer. | Customer or partner |
| Write controls | Plan authenticated tools, explicit human approval, authorization checks and audit logging for any production write; the workshop performs no writes. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Store operations owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Time associates spend finding product details, coordinating floor work and phrasing service conversations today. Establish where product search and floor coordination cost associate time before agreeing success measures.

Fill your baseline record:

| Store or department | Measurement period | Request type | Search effort | Source used | Escalations | Review owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree store replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Store operations owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Store operations owner | Approve catalog and inventory sources, audience and success measures; keep synthetic product, stock and cohort figures out of customer results. |
| Store managers and authorized associates | Review assistance drafts, store plans and coaching outputs; own policy, payment, return and personnel decisions. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and four skills; remove web search, confirm the model and keep the owned agent in Draft. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm licensing, capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before approving any store connection. |
| Commerce and inventory connection owners | Approve read-only catalog and inventory connections and the review workflow's authentication, authorization and audit controls. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check SA-01 through SA-04, the boundary tests and Easy/Manual parity; reject missing anchors and reshoot-required captures. |
| Operations owner | Own production support, session and credit monitoring and configuration recovery; route store decisions to authorized people. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Store replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures have named agreement.
- [ ] The store owner records how associates find product details, coordinate floor work and phrase service conversations today.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/store-associate-copilot/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The administrator's data policies cover the proposed catalog, inventory and review connectors, knowledge sources and intended channel; blocked routes stay blocked.
- [ ] The customer confirms authenticated audience and least-privilege access for product, price, inventory and workforce data.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/store-associate-copilot/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/store-associate-copilot/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/store-associate-copilot/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/store-associate-copilot/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Retail Store Associate Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: aibast_store-associate-rules-and-safety.md
7. Add knowledge: aibast_store-associate-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: customer-assist
9. Add skill: performance-dashboard
10. Add skill: product-lookup
11. Add skill: task-checklist
12. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
13. Open a fresh Preview conversation
14. Pass SA-01: Store Associate
15. Pass SA-02: Store Associate
16. Pass SA-03: Floor Specialist
17. Pass SA-04: Sales Manager
18. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: SA-01, SA-02, SA-03, SA-04. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, environment, model, inventory, cases and Draft state.
- [ ] If this lane is chosen, the recipe smoke test calls `StoreAssociateCopilotAgent` and returns `Product Lookup Snapshot` and `verify before advising`.
- [ ] The manual build has reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search and tools are absent.
- [ ] Each unchanged SA prompt passes once in a separate fresh Preview conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] The deterministic validator judges every case on its final response; annotated screenshots are checkpoints, not the machine gate.
- [ ] Any Easy/Manual comparison uses identical instructions, knowledge, skills, model and case identifiers.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before exposing price, inventory or workforce data. Request only the read scopes needed for approved catalog and inventory sources. Restrict the audience and test authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Approved read-only commerce catalog

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Commerce and inventory connection owners

1. **Bind Approved read-only commerce catalog — read:** Add approved read-only catalog connector actions.

2. **Identity for Approved read-only commerce catalog:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved read-only commerce catalog:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved read-only commerce catalog:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 6](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Stop and request a valid synthetic identifier; do not approximate another product. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, reservation, message or transaction succeeded.

### Step 3-2. Integrate Approved read-only store inventory

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Commerce and inventory connection owners

1. **Bind Approved read-only store inventory — read:** Add approved read-only inventory actions; keep reservation out of the agent.

2. **Identity for Approved read-only store inventory:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved read-only store inventory:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved read-only store inventory:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 1](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Reserve nothing; give the stock snapshot with `verify before advising`. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return a draft, plan or summary and name the authorized person or system.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Approved manager review workflow

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Commerce and inventory connection owners

1. **Bind Approved manager review workflow — write:** Route drafts through the approved workflow with authentication, authorization, approval and audit logging (preview).

2. **Identity for Approved manager review workflow:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved manager review workflow:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved manager review workflow:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 3](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Process no refund and send no message; offer draft language for an authorized associate. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return a draft, plan or summary and name the authorized person or system.

### Step 3-4. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Commerce and inventory connection owners

Bind only approved read-only connections and keep every write action separate.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Approved connections preserve the reviewed input and output contract; no lookup or update is claimed without tool evidence.
- [ ] Any write runs only through authenticated tools with authorization checks, explicit human approval and audit logging.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Test an approved deployment as intended store users and an unshared identity; a maker's access does not prove user access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The business owner sets customer-data acceptance measures; synthetic stock, sales and cohort figures are not thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations record the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked store corpus | All four cases, SA-01 through SA-04, include every required anchor. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, four skills and the reviewed model; no tools or web search. |
| Transaction boundary | Any reservation, promotion, message, return, refund, transaction or purchase is no-go. |
| Workforce safeguard | Any employee ranking, individual judgment or personnel decision is no-go. |
| Visual checkpoint acceptance | Require a visible positive anchor without a blocker or refusal; withhold reshoot-required captures. |
| Release state | The owned workshop agent is Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Store operations owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Store operations owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The production publish operation has explicit human confirmation.
- [ ] The approved store audience and supported channels are tested before publication is confirmed.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Store operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Store operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the reviewed workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Step 6-5. Operate

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review failed store sessions, availability promises, profiling attempts, connection errors and credit consumption in Monitor.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses a restore path supported for the environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, source usage, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.

- [ ] Build-to-operate playbooks and integrity rules.

### Customer or partner delivers

- [ ] Customer-data results, thresholds and go/no-go.
